summary:
Our team made an AI website that modifies and merges data from 2 NASA satellites: MODIS and VIIRS. By harmonizing MODIS's decade-long data with VIIRS's high-resolution imaging, our website connects critical gaps in wildfire tracking.

By using machine learning, the website automatically adjusts for false positives, upgrades old technology, accounts for sensor biases, and removes duplicate hot spots and false alarms. 

Beyond just showing active fires on a map, our tool combines multi-year burning trends and wind data to show travelling smoke toward nearby communities – turning raw datasets into actionable real-time insights that emergency responders and environmental researchers can use.Our team made an AI website that modifies and merges data from 2 NASA satellites: MODIS and VIIRS. details:
Our project uses harmonization software to synchronize the data from satellite programs VIIRS and MODIS. Before, these two data sets could not be used together, and doing so would result in double counting of fire events. If fire data were to be combined, climate data and fire prediction would be skewed for future years. This is due to the different resolution of the infrared sensors in these satellites. MODIS dates back to 2001, meaning the pixel resolution is 1km x 1km. VIIRS uses more modern sensors from 2011, and has a pixel resolution of 375m x 375m. You might wonder why we even keep the MODIS satellite active, but the data dating pre-2011, is quite useful in understanding the weather and climate in those years and also as a secondary use alongside VIIRS.

Our software synchronizes the data by visualizing the smaller VIIRS hotspots in the larger MODIS ones. To avoid miscounting, we make sure the events are in the same timestamp and in the same location. However, our software does not delete or get rid of the MODIS or VIIRS data, we include the singular satellite data alongside the harmonized points for side-by-side comparison. We have bridged a 20 year gap, and with this we could have safe communities, enhanced climate data, and save millions of dollars in infrastructure if we know where to not construct.

One of the key applications of the data synchronization is in the field of fire predictions in for potential future events. We created a down-scaled prototype that is indicative rather than predictive in terms of assessing possible future fire events. We added this as a bonus feature.
